content:
This is a classic ethical dilemma known as the trolley problem. There is no easy answer as to what the right thing to do is, as both options involve harm to individuals. 

Some may argue that pulling the lever to divert the trolley onto the side track is the more ethical option because it saves more lives overall. By taking action to save the five people on the main track, even at the cost of one person on the side track, it can be seen as maximizing the greatest good for the greatest number of people. 

On the other hand, some may argue that doing nothing is the more ethical option because it avoids directly causing harm to anyone. By not actively deciding to pull the lever and sacrificing one person, you are not violating any moral principles by actively choosing to harm someone.

Ultimately, the right thing to do in this situation is subjective and depends on individual beliefs and moral principles. It is a difficult ethical decision with no clear-cut answer, and each person may come to a different conclusion based on their own values and beliefs.
